You're producing a detailed, implementation-ready UX/design specification (a written document, not code) for Nxeon's full purchase-wizard family — a Next.js/TypeScript hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. This feeds directly into a real engineering build of an isolated portal redesign, so precision and depth matter — this is not a casual brainstorm, it needs to read like something a senior product designer at a well-funded, polished startup would hand to an engineering team.

## Context already established this session

The portal's overall redesign direction is already set: navy/violet/cyan brand hues (#6f47f5 primary violet, cyan/blue secondary accents) carried through a genuinely NEW visual system (not the current .card/.btn-* CSS), custom hand-drawn SVG icons (no icon library), Sora+Inter type pairing. Four initial mockups already exist covering: dashboard shell/nav, a VPS deploy wizard (collapsed from 5 steps to 2 — Plan, then Review & Pay — with OS/Add-ons/Access shown as expandable sections with sensible defaults rather than forced page transitions), a redesigned Billing page (tabbed), and a server detail/management page. The VPS wizard mockup already applied a "kill friction" redesign: fewer forced steps, progressive disclosure, an always-visible price summary.

There are 6 more wizard/flow components that need the same level of redesign thinking, all in `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/`:
- `HostingDeployWizard.tsx` (shared hosting)
- `GameDeployWizard.tsx` (game servers — note: I redesigned part of this earlier today, adding a trust-strip and "New"/"Popular" badges to its game-picker step specifically, but the rest of its flow — plan selection, per-game settings, review — hasn't been redesigned)
- `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`
- `DomainTransferInWizard.tsx`
- `MigrationWizard.tsx`
- `ConsolidateWizard.tsx`

All of them currently duplicate or hand-roll their own step-indicator markup (confirmed: 6 divergent implementations), and all embed the shared `PaymentStep.tsx` (except DomainTransferInWizard/MigrationWizard which don't charge). There are also existing honesty-constrained trust components you must respect: `WizardReassuranceCard.tsx`, `PaymentTrustBar.tsx`, `WizardStickyCart.tsx` — these have documented rules against fabricated guarantees/testimonials/urgency; a money-back claim was removed multiple times because no such policy is actually published. Any conversion/psychology recommendation you make must be grounded in something real and verifiable in the actual codebase/business (e.g. real uptime data, real support responsiveness, real plan value comparisons) — never invent a claim.

## Your task

Read each of the 6 wizard components (and `PaymentStep.tsx`, `WizardReassuranceCard.tsx`) thoroughly to understand their current real steps, fields, and business logic (pricing, promos, validation) — do not guess at what they do. Then produce a detailed spec, one section per wizard, covering:

1. **Current pain points** — specifically, with file:line references, what's clunky, redundant, or poorly sequenced today.
2. **Proposed new flow** — the exact new step sequence (aim for the same "collapse to the minimum real steps + progressive disclosure" philosophy as the VPS wizard), what moves to an expandable/default-assumed section, what stays a hard step.
3. **Buyer psychology applied honestly** — for each wizard, identify 1-3 SPECIFIC, real, verifiable things that could be surfaced to build purchase confidence (e.g., "Domain transfers: surface the exact real transfer-completion timeframe from the actual business logic/copy already in the codebase," "Migration: show the customer's actual current server's real specs being carried over, not a generic reassurance") — explicitly avoid generic filler like "add social proof" without a real, sourceable claim.
4. **Visual/interaction specifics** — what makes this wizard's redesign feel like a premium, coherent part of the same design system as the other four (VPS/dashboard/billing/server-detail), not a generic template. Reference specific real content from the game/domain/hosting catalog where relevant (e.g., a domain TLD picker should feel different from a game picker).

Also: propose the ONE unified `<Stepper>` component design (visual spec, not code) that should replace all 6 duplicated implementations — exact states (upcoming/current/done), exact motion on transition, how it handles a dynamic step count (e.g., DomainRegisterWizard sometimes adds an "Email" step).

This report will be read by an engineer building real React components next, so be concrete and specific, not abstract. Aim for genuine depth over breadth — better to nail 3 wizards precisely than skim all 6. Target length: as long as it needs to be for real implementation-readiness, don't artificially compress.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## 1. Full step sequence today

Steps array and stepper: `STEPS = ["Destination", "Where from", "What we found", "Review"]` at line 29. `Stepper` component at lines 152–174, driven by `step` state (`useState(0)`, line 232). Rendered dot: filled brand color if `i === step`, green checkmark "✓" if `i < step`, gray number if upcoming (lines 157–167), with a "→" arrow separator between steps (line 169). Note: `scanning` state renders a separate full-screen spinner view (lines 618–632) that hard-codes `<Stepper step={1} />` regardless of actual step.

Distinct step/screen bodies (all gated by `step === N && ...` inside one render tree, lines 634–1166):
- **Step 0 — "Choose the destination server"**: lines 643–668 (JSX), nav button "Continue →" lines 1138–1142.
- **Step 1 — "Where are you moving from?"**: lines 670–730, nav button "Scan my server →" lines 1143–1147 (triggers `runScan()`, line 283).
- **Scanning interstitial** (not in STEPS/step state, shown when `scanning===true`): lines 618–632, title "Scanning your server…".
- **Step 2 — "Here's what we found"**: lines 732–1027, nav button "Continue →" lines 1148–1152 (disabled unless `hasSelection`).
- **Step 3 — "Review & launch"**: lines 1029–1126, nav button "Start migration" / "Not enough storage" lines 1153–1162 (calls `launch()`, line 575).
- **Post-submit — `MigrationProgress`** (id-based, replaces the whole wizard once `activeId` is set, lines 611–613, 1390–1541): polling progress bar, log, and on completion either "Migration complete 🎉" (line 1503) or "Almost there — some sites need attention" (line 1491) card, plus conditionally `MigrationRemediation` (1554–1634), `PostMigrationDns` (1840–2002) and `MigrationRollback` (1689–1821).

Back button: lines 1129–1136, disabled on step 0 or while submitting.

## 2. "Detect current server" / source-server-info step

There is no dedicated "detect current server" screen with a specs summary. Step 1 ("Where from") only collects **login credentials** — it does not display any detected info about the current server (lines 670–730). Detection only happens after clicking "Scan my server →", which triggers `scanSource()` (line 283–320) and shows results on **Step 2 ("What we found")**, which is really an inventory/selection screen, not a "your current server" profile page.

What real data actually gets surfaced from the source server scan (`ScanResult`, via `scan` state):
- `scan.sourceOs` / `scan.sourceArch` — used only internally for the compatibility panel (OS family + arch), never shown as a labeled "your server's OS is X" fact by itself; surfaced indirectly inside compatibility copy, e.g. `${sa} → ${ta}` at line 482, `${FAMILY_LABEL[sFam]} → ${FAMILY_LABEL[tFam]}` at line 498, `${srcOs!.pretty || srcOs!.versionId}` at line 522.
- Disk usage of the **target**, not the source: `targetDiskFree(serverId)` (line 297) populates `targetInfo.disk` (avail/used/total) shown in `StoragePanel` (lines 1168–1344) — this is the destination server's free space, not the old server's.
- No total-disk-size/used-disk-size of the *source* server itself is shown anywhere (only per-item sizes below).
- No control-panel type (cPanel/Plesk/DirectAdmin) is asked about or detected anywhere in this file.
- No source-server IP display beyond echoing back what the customer typed (`host`) in the Review step (line 1034: `Moving from: ${user}@${host}:${port}`) and in the rollback card (`row.sourceHost`, e.g. lines 1701, 1729, 1742).
- Detected items shown in Step 2 are workload artifacts, not "server specs": web roots with per-path size labels and app-type badge (lines 793–820), running app dirs with runtime badge + size (822–851), home directories with size (853–873), detected DB engines/variants/versions (878–892, and compat items 530–567), Docker containers with images/ports/mounts (894–950), listening ports and systemd service names (952–981).
- Per-item "size" comes from `sizeLabel` strings parsed client-side (`parseSize`, lines 80–86) — this is disk usage of each folder/db, not a single "your server uses X GB of Y GB" figure for the source.

So: the wizard does NOT surface an aggregate "your current server" spec/summary card (no CPU/RAM/total-disk/control-panel/IP-geolocation summary) — it only surfaces itemized artifacts (web roots, apps, homes, DBs, containers, ports/services) plus OS family/arch used solely to drive compatibility warnings.

## 3. Fields & inputs per step

**Step 0 (Destination, lines 643–668):**
- Server picker: grid of buttons, one per `servers` prop entry, label = `s.name` (line 662). No dropdown — clickable cards. Default: `serverId = servers[0]?.id ?? ""` (line 239). Empty-state copy if `servers.length === 0`: "You don't have any servers yet. Deploy one first, then come back to migrate." (lines 650–652).

**Step 1 (Where from, lines 670–730):**
- "Old server address" text input (`host`), placeholder "203.0.113.10 or old.example.com" (lines 682–692). Validation: `hostValid = /^[a-zA-Z0-9.\-:[\]]+$/.test(host.trim())` (line 278); error text "Enter a valid IP address or domain." (line 690).
- "SSH port" text input (`port`), default `"22"` (line 242), digit-only filter (line 698), validated 1–65535 (`portValid`, line 280); error "1–65535." (line 701).
- "SSH username" text input (`user`), default `"root"` (line 243), placeholder "root" (line 707).
- "SSH password" input type=password (`password`), placeholder bullets, `autoComplete="new-password"` (lines 710–719).
- `canScan` gate: hostValid && portValid && user non-empty && password non-empty (line 281).
- No source panel type (cPanel/Plesk/DirectAdmin/custom) field exists anywhere — only raw SSH creds are collected.
- Static info box: "Databases are included automatically" — no DB password field exists; explains DBs are dumped via root SSH access (lines 722–728).

**Step 2 (What we found, lines 732–1027):** — checkboxes/toggles, not free-form fields:
- Pre-flight/prereq banner (non-interactive), storage panel, compatibility panel (see below).
- Web roots: checkbox per detected path, pre-checked (`CheckItem`, `webSel`), badge = app type (lines 793–820).
- Running apps: checkbox per app dir, pre-checked (`appSel`) (822–851).
- Home folders: checkbox per home dir, pre-checked (`homeSel`) (853–873).
- Databases: no checkboxes — informational block only, auto-included whenever an engine is detected (875–892).
- Docker containers: informational card per container + checkbox per copyable bind-mount path (`dockerSel`), pre-checked for copyable mounts (894–950).
- Ports/services: informational only, no inputs (952–981).
- "Advanced: add another folder" — `<details>` disclosure with text input `newPath` + "Add folder" button, appends to `customPaths` list, each with a "✕" remove button (983–1025). Validation: must start with "/" and not duplicate (line 331, `addPath`).
- `useVolumeForDocker` toggle lives inside `StoragePanel` (rendered on this step too) — checkbox "Use my {size} volume for Docker storage", default OFF (lines 1278–1310).

**Step 3 (Review & launch, lines 1029–1126):**
- Read-only summary rows: Destination, Moving from, Websites & folders count, Databases, "We'll install" prereqs (`Row` component, lines 1032–1048).
- File/DB list recap (1049–1058) — duplicates the same paths/engines already shown in Step 2.
- StoragePanel + CompatibilityPanel repeated again (1060–1069) — same components/state as Step 2, no new data.
- "Advanced options" disclosure (1076–1118), three safety checkboxes, all default OFF (state declared lines 266–268):
  - "Replace existing data on the destination" (`overwriteTargetData`) — sub-copy: "If the target already has a database or files with the same name, overwrite them. Off by default — we refuse and tell you instead." (lines 1081–1085).
  - "Bring up staging clones by renaming containers" (`renameClones`) — sub-copy about same-name compose stacks (1086–1091).
  - "Copy SSH authorized_keys" (`copySshKeys`) — sub-copy "public keys only — never private keys" (1092–1096).
- No destination "plan picker" or plan/cost selection UI anywhere in this file — destination is only a server picked in Step 0, not a plan.
- No migration-window/scheduling field anywhere (no date/time picker, no "schedule for later" option) — the only action is immediate "Start migration".

## 4. Migration mechanics/guarantees in the copy

Exact quotes with line refs:

- Line 625–628 (scanning screen): "We're connecting to `{host}` read-only to find your websites, files and databases. Nothing on your old server is changed. This usually takes under a minute." — **stated timeframe**: "under a minute" for the scan (not the whole migration).
- Lines 674–678 (Step 1 intro): "We'll connect over SSH and scan it for you — read-only, so nothing on your old server changes. Your password is encrypted and erased the moment the migration finishes."
- Lines 737–739 (Step 2 intro): "We migrate and start everything we can, in the same place it lived on your old server. Untick anything you don't need. Anything that needs a manual step afterwards is listed for you at the end."
- Lines 1120–1124 (Step 3 footer): "We migrate and start everything we can, in the same place it ran before — then we verify what's actually running and list anything that still needs a manual step. Nothing on your old server changes. Your SSH password is encrypted before it's stored and permanently erased once the migration finishes."
- Lines 1503–1507 ("Migration complete 🎉"): "Your files, databases and containers were copied to the same places on your Nxeon server and brought up. Check the log above for exactly what we verified running versus anything that still needs a manual step." — **no fabricated "zero downtime" or specific duration claim** here; it's phrased as verified-outcome, hedged.
- Lines 1491–1499 ("Almost there — some sites need attention", the `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` branch): "Everything was copied across, but we checked each of your domains afterwards and at least one isn't serving yet — so this move is **not finished**. ... **Your old server is untouched** — if you need to, point your DNS back to it while you sort this out." — Comment at lines 1482–1487 explicitly documents this was a fix for a real incident: showing the green complete card here previously "let a customer walk away believing they were live while their site served a certificate warning (2026-07-25)."
- Lines 1576–1579 (`MigrationRemediation` "Let us finish it for you"): "Most of the time this just means an app didn't start on its own. We can bring your apps up on the new server and re-check — no need to log in anywhere. **Nothing is down** while we do it; your old server keeps serving." — explicit no-downtime claim, scoped specifically to the remediation action (not the whole migration), and justified because it's additive server-side work while old server still serves.
- Lines 1590 ("Starting your apps and giving them a moment to boot… this can take up to a minute.") — **stated timeframe** for the "Finish setup" remediation action, not the full migration.
- Lines 1670–1688 (code comment, not user-facing, explaining the rollback design rationale) and lines 1727–1734 (`MigrationRollback` user-facing copy): "Your old server `{oldServer}` is **exactly as you left it**. This migration only ever **read** from it — we copied files, dumped databases and read its web-server configuration. Nothing there was deleted, moved, stopped, reconfigured, or switched off, and its DNS was never touched. It is still running and still able to serve your sites." — strong, specific **rollback/data-safety guarantee**, framed as a mechanical fact (read-only source access) rather than a vague marketing claim.
- Lines 1736–1749: "That means **DNS is the switch**. ... the whole move is reversible by pointing that record back ... There is nothing else to undo. We leave the new server exactly as migrated, so you can try the cutover again as soon as the problem is fixed." — explicit rollback mechanism claim.
- Lines 1815–1818: "Keep the old server running until you have seen the new one serve real traffic. Once you are happy, cancel it with your old provider — that is the only step in this whole process that cannot be undone." — honest hedge naming the one irreversible step.

**Overall assessment on HONESTY scrutiny**: None of these read as a fabricated/unbacked guarantee in the way the codebase's pattern seems to police (per the `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` comment at 1482–1487, this codebase has actively removed/fixed a case where UI overstated success). The claims present (read-only source access, no data deleted, DNS-is-the-switch rollback, "nothing is down" during remediation) all appear to be grounded in the actual mechanics described in code comments (e.g., lines 1670–1688 explain exactly why: rsync-pull, dump via local socket, read-only config read, no DNS writes). There is **no overall stated migration duration** ("your migration will take X hours") anywhere in the wizard — the only timeframes quoted are "under a minute" for the scan (line 628) and "up to a minute" for the finish-setup boot step (line 1590). No SLA, no "zero-downtime cutover" claim for the full migration itself (DNS cutover inherently has propagation delay, and the copy at lines 1888–1889 honesty-hedges this: "Expect a few minutes before everyone sees the change — keep the old server up until then.").

## 5. PaymentStep integration

`PaymentStep` is **not imported, referenced, or rendered anywhere** in this file (confirmed via full read — no "Payment", "payment", "price", "cost", "$", "checkout", or "invoice" tokens appear in the 2003 lines except as described below). # Nxeon Wizard Family — Implementation-Ready Redesign Spec

Scope: the 6 remaining wizard/flow components in `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/` — `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`, `GameDeployWizard.tsx`, `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`, `DomainTransferInWizard.tsx`, `MigrationWizard.tsx`, `ConsolidateWizard.tsx` — plus the one unified `<Stepper>` that should replace all 6 divergent implementations. Every fact below was pulled from the actual files (line numbers cited); every psychology recommendation is sourced to a real, verifiable claim already present in the codebase or its business logic — nothing invented.

---

## Part 0 — The Unified `<Stepper>` Component

### Why it has to be one component

Confirmed 6-way divergence:
- `HostingDeployWizard.tsx:68–90` — own `Stepper`, circular badges, ✓ for done, no shared import.
- `GameDeployWizard.tsx:169–192` — a second, near-identical `Stepper`, whose own comment says "matching the VPS DeployWizard" — i.e. it's explicitly copy-pasted styling, not shared code.
- `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx:63–85` — a third copy, accepts a `steps` prop (needed because its step count is 4 or 5 depending on `freeInboxPlan`, lines 139–141).
- `DomainTransferInWizard.tsx:40–62` — a fourth copy, hardcoded to its own module-level `STEPS` constant rather than a prop — structurally identical markup to #3 but literally un-shareable as written.
- `MigrationWizard.tsx:152–174` — a fifth copy, with a real bug: the scanning interstitial hardcodes `<Stepper step={1} />` regardless of the actual step state (line ~620).
- `ConsolidateWizard.tsx` — no stepper at all; three real phases (setup → scan/plan → run/result) communicated only through prose and button-label changes.

One component, `<Stepper steps={string[]} current={number} variant?="default"|"muted" />`, fixes all of this and gives every wizard the same spine.

### Visual states

**Badge** — 28×28px circle, 1.5px border, centered numeral or glyph:
- **Upcoming**: `border-white/10`, numeral in `text-slate-500`, background transparent. No glow.
- **Current**: `border-brand-400` (violet), background `bg-brand-500/15`, numeral in `text-brand-200`, plus a soft outer ring (`ring-2 ring-brand-500/25`) that gives a barely-perceptible ambient pulse (2.4s ease-in-out, opacity 0.6→1→0.6) — enough to draw the eye without feeling like a loading spinner.
- **Done**: fill transitions to a violet→cyan diagonal gradient border (`border-transparent`, gradient via `background-clip`), numeral cross-fades to a checkmark glyph. **Deliberately not emerald.** Emerald is already the platform's reserved color for *financial* success (wallet credits, discount badges, "available" domain pills — confirmed across `PaymentStep.tsx`, `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`, `WizardReassuranceCard.tsx`). Giving step-completion its own violet/cyan identity keeps "I finished a step" visually distinct from "you saved money" or "this is available," rather than diluting emerald into a catch-all success color.

**Connector** — replace every current wizard's literal `→` text glyph with a real 2px horizontal line between badges. Unfilled segment: `bg-white/8`. As a step completes, its trailing segment fills left-to-right with the same violet→cyan gradient as the Done badge — the line becomes a genuine progress bar, not decoration between icons.

**Label** — Sora Medium, 12px, positioned under (desktop) or beside (mobile) the badge. Upcoming: `text-slate-500`. Current: `text-slate-100` (brightest point in the row — deliberately drawing more attention than the Done labels, which dim back to `text-slate-400` once passed, so focus stays on "where am I now," not "look how far I've come").

**Ambient progress rail** — a 2px accent bar spanning the full width of the wizard card, positioned directly above the Stepper row, width = `(current + 1) / steps.length * 100%`, same gradient fill. This is a peripheral-vision cue independent of the badge row — useful on mobile's collapsed variant where individual badges aren't shown.

### Motion on transition

Forward (Continue clicked, `current` increases):
1. `t=0ms`: outgoing current badge begins its Current→Done morph — numeral cross-fades to checkmark (150ms), border animates from solid violet to the gradient, outer ring fades out.
2. `t=50ms`: the connector segment trailing that badge begins its fill sweep, 250ms ease-out, so the "energy" visibly travels forward from the badge that just completed.
3. `t=150ms`: the new current badge scales in from 0.92→1.0 (180ms, ease-out) with its ring fading in over the same window.
4. Labels cross-fade color in sync with their badges (no separate timing).
Total perceived transition: ~380ms. This should read as a small, satisfying "this step is locked in" moment — the closest thing this system has to a micro-celebration, appropriate for a purchase flow.

Backward (Back clicked, `current` decreases): **no sweep, no scale-in** — a flat 120ms opacity/color cross-fade only. Going back is neutral, not an achievement in reverse; animating it the same way as forward progress would cheapen the forward animation's meaning.

`variant="muted"` (for `ConsolidateWizard`, see its section): same states and colors, but the forward transition drops to the flat 120ms cross-fade used for Back everywhere else — no gradient sweep, no ring pulse. This tool has no purchase moment; its step completions are operational progress, not milestones worth celebrating visually.

### Dynamic step count

Confirmed: no wizard changes its step count *mid-session* — `DomainRegisterWizard`'s "Email" step is decided once, from a server-provided prop (`freeInboxPlan`), before the customer starts. So `<Stepper>` itself never needs to animate a length change; it always receives a `steps` array that's stable for the life of the mount, computed once at the top of the parent wizard.

That said, the *reason* the array needs to vary at all (a feature toggle changing what steps exist) is itself a smell worth designing away — see the DomainRegisterWizard section below, where the recommendation is to make that specific case moot by turning the conditional step into conditional *content* inside a fixed step instead. `<Stepper>` should support a variable-length `steps` prop for whichever wizard still legitimately needs it, but the target end-state is that none of the six do.

### Responsive behavior

- **Desktop (≥768px)**: full row — badge + label under each, connectors between.
- **Mobile (<768px)**: collapses to a single horizontal dot-track (8px dots, no numerals) plus one text line to its right showing only the current step's label and position: `Plan · Step 2 of 4`. The ambient progress rail above it becomes the primary progress cue at this width.

### Fixing the "Change" inconsistency this unifies

Across three files (`HostingDeployWizard.tsx:750` vs `:920`; `GameDeployWizard.tsx:1247` vs `:1336–1351`; `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`'s two Review branches), "change this earlier choice" currently means two different things in the same wizard: sometimes a hard `setStep(0)` jump back to page one, sometimes an inline reveal in place. Adopting the unified Stepper should come with one interaction rule enforced everywhere: **no control on the Review/Pay step ever calls `setStep()`.** Every "Change"/"Edit" affordance on the last step opens an inline reveal (the relevant picker slides open in place, price recalculates live, "Done" collapses it again) — never a full navigation event. This single rule retires `onEdit: () => setStep(0)` (Hosting `:923`, Game's equivalent, Domain Register's `:704`) everywhere it appears.

This is structurally different from the other five: no payment leg, no `PaymentStep`, a technical/ops audience (people running their own SSH-reachable servers), and today it isn't a wizard at all — a single-page form with phases distinguished only by what has conditionally rendered below the fold.
